newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on overbought signals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on overbought signals.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on late speculative selling, centered in the March contract, with signals the market was overbought technically leading the way down, traders said.

"It just got overbought. The world production numbers came out Tuesday and they (traders) were paying too much attention to that and not enough to domestic values which weren't keeping pace (with the futures rally)," a trader said.
USDA Tuesday trimmed its estimate for the 1996-97 world and U.S. wheat carryout. Wheat rallied Tuesday and Wednesday but buying dried up as December moved above $4.00 per bushel, a three-week high.
The drop in prices Thursday occurred despite a more optimistic outlook for U.S. wheat exports including a cut by the EU in its export subsidy for wheat.
"Egypt is in over the weekend for French and maybe some U.S. wheat and we're waiting for the (USDA weekly) export sales tomorrow," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Traders were expecting USDA's weekly export sales data Friday to show wheat net sales at 300,000 to 350,000 tonnes.
Wheat closed unchanged to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down four at $3.96-3/4.
The late drop in wheat futures also was tied to ideas that most of the recent bullish export news already had been factored into the market.
There has been speculation Egypt may tender for up to 300,000 tonnes of wheat over the weekend and there have been hints Egypt may purchase some wheat from the U.S.

Traders took note of the European Union's cut in its restitution refund offered exporters to 15.97 ECUS for wheat and a cut to 22 ECUS for soft wheat flour exports. Last week the refunds were 22.35 ECUS and 27 ECUS, respectively.
Support to futures also came from news Turkey planned to cut its 15-percent tax on wheat imports. There has been talk Turkey may soon buy up to 500,000 tonnes of wheat.
Refco Inc, Griffin Trading, Rand Financial and Cargill Inc were said the key sellers in the March during the waning minutes of trading.

The nearby December was giving off definite signals of an overbought near term market with the daily relative strength index (RSI) moving to 64 points at Wednesday's close, with Thursday's close at 59. Traders view an RSI of 70 or more as an overbought market and 30 or less as oversold.
Technicians also said the key moving averages remain bearish.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 13,500 contracts, below the 22,561 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
Wheat options volume was light with Paine Webber a purchaser of 75 March $3.80 puts at 10 cents and First Options sold 75 December $3.90 puts at 1/2 cent, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 6,000 contracts, below the 7,355 traded Wednesday.
